Within a single evaluation, evidence of mere checklist compliance tracking the right answer is observed when the panel fails on out-of-distribution cases where expert intuition generalizes but checklist rules do not.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The evaluation is restricted to in-distribution cases where the checklist is perfectly specified, hiding the expert's generalization advantage.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel successfully modifies or abandons the checklist when encountering out-of-distribution cases, demonstrating meta-cognitive monitoring rather than rigid compliance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Expert intuition operates on a high-dimensional, non-verbalizable feature space (System 1 pattern recognition) that cannot be fully captured by a low-dimensional explicit checklist. For tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes, the expert's unformalizable tacit knowledge allows them to generalize to novel cases, while the panel is rigidly constrained by the checklist's bounded scope. Therefore, the expert will outperform on edge cases.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
